plan: Sell all SOXL and SPAL to eliminate leveraged ETF risk.
Trim SMH to 5% and SPY to 20% to reduce sector and index concentration.
Add QQQI to 20% to increase income-generating assets.
Trim CRWD to 10% to further reduce single-name concentration.

conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for lower, steadier returns (~1.5%/mo) by significantly reducing risk. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also capped upside potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to address concentration and leverage.
Reduce SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to manage leveraged ETF risk.
Add CRWD to 10% to increase exposure to a high-scoring name.
Trim QQQI slightly to 10% to rebalance towards growth.
This plan balances risk reduction with targeted growth opportunities.
balanced.read: This balanced strategy targets moderate growth (~2.5%/mo) with a focus on risk management. It aims to reduce concentration and leverage while selectively adding to strong performers.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to reduce broad index concentration.
Add SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6% to increase leveraged ETF exposure.
Add CRWD to 10% to further concentrate on a strong performer.
Buy AAPL and ADI at 5% each to add high-scoring tech names.
This aggressive plan seeks maximum growth by increasing leverage and concentration in top setups.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for high growth (~4%/mo) by embracing leverage and concentration. Expect significantly higher potential upside but also substantially larger drawdowns and amplified losses, especially with leveraged ETFs.

plan: Sell all SOXL, SPAL, SMH, and CRWD to exit high-risk and growth-oriented positions.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad market exposure.
Increase QQQI to 40% to maximize income generation.
Buy JEPQ at 20% to add another income-focused ETF.
This plan prioritizes stable monthly income and capital preservation over growth.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets steady monthly distributions (~1%/mo) with minimal volatility. It prioritizes capital preservation and reliable income over aggressive growth, accepting lower potential upside.
